subject: Reserved pool regrade: A100 → H100/L40S — performance-per-dollar case & term amendment
messages:
From: Samir Hussein <samir@atlas-ai.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Atlas AI Procurement <procurement@atlas-ai.com>

Subject: Capacity renewal discussion — A100 pool needs & timeline

Tessa / Marissa,

Quick note from our side as we head into renewal: our production model footprint has spiked ~45% over the last quarter. We're currently on a 20x A100 reserved pool with Redwood and seeing contention during peak hours. Procurement asked us to explore upgrading to newer hardware (H100 or L40S) to get better throughput per dollar and reduce tail latency.

Key asks from Atlas:
- Can Redwood provide a clear PPD (performance-per-dollar) comparison A100 → H100 (and L40S) for our workload?
- We need options for adding capacity (+8 to +12 GPUs) and an accelerated path if we commit to 12–24 months.
- Throughput guarantee (e.g., sustained tokens/sec baseline) and a simple SLA credit table for drops below target.
- Procurement timeline: aim to sign amendment by Oct 22 to have capacity available before Black Friday-like traffic.

Can you send a short economics case and a recommended commitment option? We prefer a concise one-pager + spreadsheet.

Thanks — Samir
Samir Hussein
Head of Infrastructure, Atlas AI
[Attachment: sample-usage.csv]

- I will assemble a short PPD comparison and propose two commitment options (12m vs 24m) with pricing and throughput guarantees.
- Internally I'll loop in Marissa for pricing and Ben for capacity/config details.

Can you confirm whether we should model a full swap of the 20 A100s, or a hybrid approach (e.g., replace 12 A100s with H100 and keep 8 as L40S/optimized A100s)? That will change the TCO math.

I'll follow up with an internal note and a formal proposal within 48 hours.

— Tessa

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-07T10:25:00-07:00
Subject: internal: Atlas AI — regrade options & PPD summary

Team — summary for Atlas (they asked for a concise econ case + options). Attached workbook has full calc (redwood_h100_tco_calc.xlsx). High-level bullets: 

Workload assumptions (from Atlas sample): steady-state batch + bursty infer ops, median seq 512 tokens, 95th around 2048.

PPD / perf deltas (modeled):
- H100 (sustained): ~1.8x throughput vs A100 on their average sequence mix; raw hardware $/hour ~2.1x A100 but net $/token improves ~35% after batching & KV cache gains.
- L40S (quantized path): slightly lower raw throughput but ~30% lower $/token vs A100 for long-context workloads when quantized int8 is viable.
- Hybrid swap (12 H100 + 8 L40S): modeled as best balance for tail latency and unit cost — delivers ~33% reduction in $/token vs current pool.

Operational notes:
- Migration risk: KV cache warm-up will cost initial latency and token duplication; we estimate a 36–48 hour warm-up window for peak efficiency.
- Fallbacks: plan a policy route that can spill requests back to A100 pool for non-latency sensitive traffic during migration peaks.
- Throughput SLA: propose a baseline throughput metric (tokens/sec) per pool with 99% availability target; credit step-downs if we miss the sustained baseline for >30 min.

Commercial options for Atlas (sketch):
1) 12-month amendment: +10 H100 reserved (full swap of 10/20), price uplift +28% vs current commit; no upfront discount; includes 72 hours of premium migration support and 5% credit cap for SLA misses.
2) 24-month amendment: +12 H100 (or hybrid 12 H100 + 8 L40S), price uplift +18% vs current commit effective monthly; includes deeper per-unit discount, 120 hours migration support, and a 2.5% credit cap + guaranteed throughput band.

Requesting Marissa for exact list price / committed rate for both options and Ben for availability windows (region: us-west). Neha, can you verify if SOC2 evidence or any security scoping is needed for the additional capacity?

Thanks — Tessa
[Attachment: redwood_h100_tco_calc.xlsx]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Adding preliminary commercial numbers (sketch for internal use):
- 12m option (add 10 H100): committed rate = $2.10/hr equivalent per H100 (blended), estimated blended $/token down 30% vs current. Migration support add-on = $18k. SLA credit table included in attached draft.
- 24m option (12 H100 + 8 L40S hybrid): committed rate = $1.75/hr equivalent per H100 (blended after term), blended $/token down ~36%. Migration support and 24/7 coordination included.

Ben — availability note: we have limited H100 headroom in us-west for Nov; earliest full-dedicated delivery for +12 H100 is late-Nov unless we reserve now. Recommend pushing procurement to sign by Oct 22 for guaranteed Nov rollout.

I'll convert this into a short PDF offer and send to Tessa to share with Atlas.

— Marissa

Subject: Proposal: reserved pool regrade & commitment options (summary)

Samir / Procurement / Elena — attaching our concise offer and the model. Two practical paths: 12-month commit (fast lane) or 24-month commit (best unit economics). Summary below: 

Option A — 12-month (fast lane)
- Add +10 H100 (swap 10 of 20 A100s)
- Blended uplift: +28% vs current monthly spend
- Throughput guarantee: sustained baseline X tokens/sec (detailed in PDF). SLA credits up to 5% of monthly invoice if sustained baseline missed >30 min.
- Migration window: 2–3 weeks with 72h priority support.

Option B — 24-month (economy optimum)
- Add +12 H100 and convert 8 A100 → L40S hybrid
- Blended uplift: +18% vs current monthly spend; effective $/token down ~36%
- Throughput guarantee: higher sustained baseline; SLA credits capped at 2.5% for extended outages.
- Migration window: staged rollout across 3 weeks + full migration runbook and 120h of dedicated SRE support.

Attachments: reservedpool_regrade_offer_v1.pdf, redwood_h100_tco_calc.xlsx

Next step: which option would you like priced into an amendment? If both, we can prepare a single DocuSign amendment with checkboxes. Target signature date per your timeline is Oct 22.

— Tessa

Subject: Re: Proposal: reserved pool regrade & commitment options (summary)

Tessa — thank you. A few clarifying Qs from procurement/infra before we escalate to legal: 
1) During migration, can we route a percentage of traffic back to existing A100 pool (rollback) with no additional charge? What are the throttling/queueing effects?
2) Can you confirm KV cache migration plan? Will we lose effective cache hits for X hours?
3) If H100 supply is constrained, are we able to do a partial immediate upgrade (e.g., +6 H100 in Nov, remainder in Jan) and still get the 24m pricing?

If you can answer these, we'll schedule a short procurement call and get terms to legal.

— Samir

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
To: Samir Hussein <samir@atlas-ai.com>, Atlas AI Procurement <procurement@atlas-ai.com>, Elena Ruiz <elena@atlas-ai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-09T15:46:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Proposal: reserved pool regrade & commitment options (summary)

Samir — answers below, and I'll paste the short rollback/runbook notes for procurement/legal.

1) Route-back / rollback: yes — we can route a defined percentage of production traffic to your existing A100 pool during migration windows with no extra per-request charge. We will throttle to preserve tail latency; this may increase queue depth and raise p95/p99 for those requests we spill, so it's best used for background/non-critical jobs. We'll build a traffic policy you can toggle from the console and include a 2-hour failover playbook.

2) KV cache migration: expected warm-up loss — roughly 36–48 hours before cache reaches steady hit-rate for hot prefixes. During that period we expect ~10–18% increase in egress tokens and slightly higher latency for cache-miss dominated requests. We'll include a pre-warm plan (synthetic warmers) to reduce that window.

3) Phased delivery & pricing: we can support phased delivery (+6 now, remainder later) and will honor the 24m pricing if the full commit is documented in the amendment and the schedule is within the agreed rollout window (Nov–Jan). If the phased delay extends beyond the agreed window, pricing may be re-calculated.

Runbook snippet (for legal/procurement):
- Amendment covers the committed pool size and term; phase-in schedule attached as an exhibit.
- SLA: baseline tokens/sec defined per pool; credits accrue when baseline not met for >30 consecutive minutes; max monthly credit cap defined per option.
- Migration support: priority SRE hours and on-call window for cutover.
- Fallback: policy-controlled spillback to A100 pool; no additional charge for routing during the migration window.

I can send a draft amendment + DocuSign link by EOD if you confirm Option B (24m) or Option A (12m).

Regards,
Tessa
